$comment: Sidecar binary hashes. These do NOT verify upstream -- only the PGP signature in scripts/build-sidecar.sh does that. They exist so CI can detect when a rebuild drifts from what was reviewed and recorded here.

source.$comment: ffmpeg.org publishes a .asc signature, not a .sha256 file (verified: the .sha256 URL returns 404). The signature is the upstream check; this hash is recorded for reproducibility.

license.auditedBy: scripts/build-sidecar.sh greps -buildconf for enable-gpl, enable-nonfree, libx264, libx265 and libfdk, and fails the build if any is present
license.result: CLEAN: no GPL or nonfree components linked

verification.$comment: A successful link and a clean licence audit are not evidence a binary works. Three builds passed both and still failed on their first real command.
verification.smokeTest: encode 1s of testsrc2 to VP9, then ffprobe it and assert codec_name == vp9

h264DecodeTest.note: An H.264 file produced by the system ffmpeg was decoded and transcoded by this sidecar. H.264 *decoding* -- what import and preview need -- is fully functional. Only H.264 *encoding* is absent.

ffmpeg-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.status: REVIEWED: licence audit clean, smoke test passed, H.264 decode verified

ffprobe-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.status: REVIEWED: licence audit clean, smoke test passed

capabilities.$comment: What this build can and cannot do. The encode gap is the visible cost of ADR-006 being open.

missing.h264Encoder: libx264 is GPL. Excluded while ADR-006 is open. Export falls back to VP9/AV1.
missing.hevcEncoder: libx265 is GPL. Excluded for the same reason.
missing.av1Encoder: libsvtav1 has no Debian 13 package; would need a second pinned source build.
missing.note: None of these affect decoding, which is what import and preview require.

windows.$comment: Built by CI under MSYS2 with the same configure line. No Windows machine needed to produce a Windows package.
